Regional autism-associated gene candidates

Scope: the app’s existing 20-gene protein library. These results are not a genome-wide ranking, a diagnosis, an ASD/control contrast, or a measure of causal importance.

Genetic evidence

Eligible genes have SFARI score 1 (High Confidence) or 2 (Strong Candidate) in the official Human Gene table retrieved 28 October 2026. Genetic categories and report counts are retained. Report counts and syndromic status are not ranking weights. SFARI provides evidence about association overall, not region-specific causal evidence. The archived source page, exact selected rows and checksum are preserved in the project research folder.

Sample-weighted regional enrichment

Pool individual tissue-sample nTPM values across the target source entries and give each unique sample ID one equal vote. Divide that mean by the mean of individual tissue samples across all other source entries with verified sample rows in the SAME study. Deduplicate IDs within the study; remove every target ID from the baseline. Repeated IDs with conflicting values fail the build. There is no equal-area fallback and missing counts are never invented.

All 193 HPA brain source areas have sample records for all 20 library genes. The separate HPA prefrontal study has verified sample records for all 20 areas. Six parietal cortex tissue records per gene were recovered from the separate official parietal cortex page and checked against the saved source summary. Each candidate lists baseline coverage, excluded areas and target/comparison tissue counts. The two studies are not pooled.

Require a tissue-sample mean ≥1 nTPM and ≥1.25-fold enrichment. Sort by enrichment, then regional sample mean, then gene symbol. Show up to three qualifying candidates. These are descriptive interface thresholds, not significance tests or diagnostic rules.

TBR1 postcentral example

The source entries contain 1, 6, 5 and 3 tissue samples. Their contributions are now 6.7%, 40.0%, 33.3% and 20.0%, rather than 25% each. The mean of the 15 individual sample measurements is 78.493 nTPM, compared with the former equal-area mean of 85.175 nTPM. Original entry means (105.0, 65.1, 84.8 and 85.8) remain available for provenance. Small rounding differences are expected because the calculation uses individual sample rows, not rounded entry means.

The same-study comparison contains 951 other tissue samples across 189 source areas, with mean 23.342 nTPM, giving 3.363× enrichment. The 15 target samples are excluded from the comparison.

Limits

nTPM means normalized transcripts per million and measures RNA, not protein. The means are across individual tissue samples, not independent donors. Tissue samples can differ in anatomical size and biological composition, and repeated samples from one donor can still influence the result. No uncertainty intervals or cell-type, age or donor adjustments are available here. Reference-brain expression does not establish autism-specific dysregulation.

Adult atlas parcels map by anatomical names, not a registration of measurements to this brain. Related or broader matches can cause multiple parcels to share the same source values and rankings. Left and right use identical expression evidence. A broadly expressed gene such as NRXN1 may still qualify where its regional enrichment meets the rule.

Audit and sources

Rankings, formula and genetic evidence · Underlying mapped HPA values · HPA studies, anatomical crosswalk, licensing and attribution. The reproducible build uses preserved complete per-gene source-area tables, including areas outside the visible cortex.
